solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Page taking another right turn around vault

parts.note: a leaf is a page of a book
another page, abbreviated P, goes inside LEAF
R = right
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A page boy takes another right turn on his way round a burial vault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vault' looks like a noun (a crypt), but it is the playground game in which you vault over a crouching friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapfrog is a game of vaulting over others, and also a verb meaning to vault over.

clue.text: Runaway inmate stops here at last to cover head

indicators.note: take the last letter of each of the words before it
the outer letters wrap around, covering, the next piece

parts.note: last letters of inmatE, stopS, herE
a cape or head is a headland, as in Beachy Head

explanation.surface: A prison story: the runaway inmate's journey finally ends here, head hidden under a hood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runaway inmate' reads as one phrase, but only 'Runaway' is the definition; 'inmate' is the first of the three words whose last letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A runaway, as a noun, is someone who has fled, which is an escapee.

clue.text: Blunt scheme collecting one small parking fine inside of Kent

parts.note: a scheme is a plan
one = I, the Roman numeral, placed inside PLAN
S = small, as on clothing labels
P = parking, as on road signs
fine = OK

indicators.note: only the inner letters of Kent are used

parts.note: the middle letters of KENT

explanation.surface: A heavy-handed scheme to collect small parking fines within Kent, a county in south-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' is not a penalty here, despite the parking; it simply means OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone plain-spoken says things bluntly, without softening them.

clue.text: What flows up through hollow rusty piping

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the piece reads from the bottom, backwards
the reversed river runs through the other letters, sitting inside them

parts.note: the outer letters of RUSTY

indicators.note: rusty with its middle emptied leaves only its outer letters

parts.note: the Dee is a river, a thing that flows

explanation.surface: Water trickling up through a corroded, empty old pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piping' seems to be plumbing to match 'rusty', but it is an adjective for a high, thin voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A piping voice is high and thin, which is what a reedy voice is.

clue.text: Cook's high-quality cheese with 40 per cent off king paid for

indicators.note: two of GOUDA's five letters, 40 per cent, are cut off the end

parts.note: GOUDA, a Dutch cheese, less its last two letters
R = rex, king
to meet a bill is to pay it, so met = paid for

explanation.surface: A cook's fine cheese, marked down forty per cent, is bought by the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook's high-quality' reads as the start of a story, but it defines the answer: gourmet food is the high-quality kind a cook serves.
explanation.definitionFit: Gourmet, as an adjective, describes high-quality food for discerning eaters and cooks.

clue.text: Engage contractors with globe

parts.note: abs, the abdominal muscles, contract
an orb is a globe

explanation.surface: Hiring builders to work on a globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contractors' suggests builders, but here it means muscles, which are the body's contractors.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage someone's attention is to absorb them in something.

clue.text: Disdain old guy's first shown in island church

indicators.note: OG appears inside the island's name

parts.note: Arran is an island off the west coast of Scotland

indicators.note: take only the first letter of guy

parts.note: O = old
the first letter of GUY; O and G go inside ARRAN
CE = Church of England

explanation.surface: An old man's scorn, shown first in a little island church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old guy's first' splits in two: 'old' gives O on its own and 'first' applies only to guy, so OG, not just G, goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain is contempt for others, which is arrogance.

clue.text: Type of music request when cycling

parts.note: to request is to ask

explanation.surface: Asking for a song while riding a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' sounds like bicycles; it means moving the first letter to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Ska is a Jamaican style of music, forerunner of reggae.

clue.text: Whistler may display this in town close to Sunderland

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside town in north-east England

indicators.note: the close, or end, of Sunderland is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of SUNDERLAND

explanation.surface: A whistling painter shows off his work in a town near Sunderland, a city in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistler' invites the painter James Whistler, but it is a football referee, who blows a whistle and shows a red card.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee, the whistler, holds up a red card to send a player off.

clue.text: Cut in drab uniform fixed after two drinks

indicators.note: the letters are fixed, as in repaired, into a new order
the rearranged letters come after the two drinks

parts.note: CHA, slang for tea, then TEA itself
IN + DRAB + U (uniform in the phonetic alphabet), rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier in a dull uniform, tidied up after a couple of drinks, gets a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a trim, but it is a cut of meat: the thick centre of a beef fillet.
explanation.definitionFit: Chateaubriand is a thick cut from the tenderloin of beef.

clue.text: Just about record somersaulting in public

parts.note: just = only
an EP is an extended-play record; reversed and put inside ONLY

explanation.surface: An acrobat very nearly sets a tumbling record in front of a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just about' looks like one phrase meaning nearly, but 'Just' is ONLY and 'about' says it goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what is done in public is done where all can see, not in secret.

clue.text: Celebrity recalled some philosopher at sage meeting

indicators.note: called back, so the letters read backwards
only some of the letters of the phrase are used

parts.note: philosopheR AT SAGE Meeting, read backwards

explanation.surface: A famous figure remembers a gathering where a thinker met a wise man.
explanation.walkthrough: The thinkers are there only to carry letters; a megastar is about as far from a sage as the clue gets.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with MEGA- adding scale: a star of the biggest kind is a celebrity.

clue.text: Means of driving forward, except for earlier Tesla models

parts.note: stimulations spur things on
T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density; the first T is removed

explanation.surface: Talk of how cars are driven, apart from Tesla's early models.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car maker, with 'models' and 'driving' to match; here it is the scientific unit, symbol T.
explanation.definitionFit: Simulations are models that imitate how something behaves.

clue.text: Port resident docked close to ace pilot flying north

indicators.note: NEAR has its tail docked, cut off
the letters are sent flying into a new order

parts.note: close to = NEAR, minus its last letter
A (ace, as on playing cards) + PILOT, rearranged
N = north

explanation.surface: A harbour resident has moored by a top pilot who flies northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docked' wants to belong to the port, but it trims the word after it. 'Resident' belongs with 'Port' in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Neapolitan lives in Naples, a port city in southern Italy.

clue.text: One working for lender in Iran worked with Blair

indicators.note: the letters are worked, as in kneaded, into a new shape

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder, mixed in with IRAN

explanation.surface: A bank employee in Iran collaborated with Tony Blair, the former British prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lender' suggests a bank, but a library lends books.
explanation.definitionFit: A librarian works for a library, an institution that lends books.

clue.text: Government department introducing current PM

parts.note: MOD = Ministry of Defence
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A ministry introduces the sitting prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like it qualifies PM, meaning the present one, but it is I. Narendra Modi is prime minister of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Narendra Modi is a PM, India's prime minister.

clue.text: A lot of muck on left side of Kelvin's Highland sticker

indicators.note: most, but not all, of DIRT is used

parts.note: DIRT less its last letter

indicators.note: in an across word the left side is the first letter

parts.note: the first letter of KELVIN

explanation.surface: Mud all over the left side of Kelvin's Scottish souvenir sticker.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'sticker' sounds like a label, but it is something you stick people with: a dirk is a Scottish Highland dagger.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirk is a long dagger traditionally carried in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Six blocking opening that's artificially produced

parts.note: an intro is the opening of a piece
VI is six in Roman numerals, placed inside INTRO

explanation.surface: A cricket six blocks an opening that was manufactured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artificially produced' is an adjective phrase, and IN VITRO works the same way, as in in vitro fertilisation.
explanation.definitionFit: In vitro means made in a test tube or dish, outside the body, so artificially produced.

clue.text: Male band saving time with Bill's great deal

parts.note: a buck is a male deer or rabbit
ELO, the Electric Light Orchestra, a British rock band
T = time, placed inside ELO
a bill, a poster, is an advertisement, an AD

explanation.surface: A boy band saves time while getting a bargain from Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill's' reads as possessive, but the 's is just 'is': Bill is (the) great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom: as much as a bucket holds stands for a large amount.

clue.text: Natives of foreign ancestry broadcast scoreline having lost at home

indicators.note: the letters are scattered, like seed broadcast over a field

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged, once IN is gone
to be in is to be at home; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A foreign-born team's supporters hear a result read out after an away defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' seems to go with the scoreline on the radio, but it only rearranges letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Creoles are people born in the Caribbean or Americas of European or mixed ancestry.

clue.text: Did Harry duck Yankee visiting old queen and duke?

parts.note: Queen Anne reigned in the early 1700s
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
Yankee is Y in the phonetic alphabet; O and Y go inside ANNE
D = duke

explanation.surface: A royal question: did Prince Harry dodge an American visiting the old queen and a duke?
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like the prince, surrounded by queens and dukes, but 'harry' is a verb meaning to pester, so 'Did Harry' means annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to harass them, so 'did harry' is annoyed.

clue.text: Eggs on hosts smashing new dishes

indicators.note: one piece placed next to the other
something smashed is broken into pieces, so the letters of new lose their order

parts.note: ova are eggs
NEW rearranged, placed inside OVA
re = on, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone egging on party hosts to smash the new crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eggs on' reads as a verb, urging; it is really OVA + RE, with 'on' doing double duty as the RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovenware is heat-proof dishes for cooking in the oven.

clue.text: Affectionate daughter books popular centre for vigil

parts.note: D = daughter
OT = Old Testament, a set of books
in = popular, fashionable

indicators.note: only the middle letter of vigil is used

parts.note: the middle letter of VIGIL

explanation.surface: A loving daughter reserves a well-liked venue for a candlelit vigil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books' looks like a verb, reserving a venue; it is OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Doting means fondly, excessively affectionate.

clue.text: Old bit of school out of bounds

parts.note: to school someone is to educate them; drop the E at each end

explanation.surface: A former part of a school that pupils are no longer allowed into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit' looks like a part, but it is a coin, as in a threepenny bit, an old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A ducat was an old gold or silver coin, so an old bit of money.

clue.text: Part of terrorist organisation isn't backing Mike in play Operation

parts.note: a terrorist group is organised in cells
isn't expanded to IS NOT
to play is to toy
Mike is M in the phonetic alphabet, placed inside TOY

explanation.surface: A terrorist cell refuses to back Mike in a play called 'Operation'.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital O makes 'Operation' look like a title, but it is a surgical operation. 'Isn't' must be spelt out as IS NOT before reversing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsillectomy is the surgical operation to remove the tonsils.

clue.text: Granny periodically reared Jade

indicators.note: take every other letter, at regular periods
in a down clue, reared means raised up, read from the bottom

parts.note: the odd letters of GrAnNy

explanation.surface: Grandmother, from time to time, brought up a girl named Jade.
explanation.walkthrough: Jade reads as a girl's name, but a jade is a worn-out old horse, which is a nag.
explanation.definitionFit: A jade is an old, worn-out horse, which is also called a nag.

clue.text: Bean drink paired with game

parts.note: nog is an egg-based drink, as in eggnog
gin rummy, the card game, is often just gin

explanation.surface: A coffee bean drink served with a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bean' looks like coffee, but it is slang for the head, as is noggin.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean and noggin are both informal words for the head.

clue.text: Reserve awkwardly eats second fish

indicators.note: the letters of eats are arranged awkwardly, out of order

parts.note: EATS rearranged
S = second
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A substitute player clumsily eats a second helping of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' looks like a noun, a substitute player, but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: keeping something back for later use.
